integrated_description: Before disclosing diagnostic uncertainty, assess the patient's preference for level of detail and tailor the depth of disclosure to both that preference and the clinical risk or urgency of the situation, ensuring higher-stakes uncertainty receives more explicit communication while immediate treatment contexts may use lighter framing. Structure the disclosure to clearly distinguish what is most likely from what is less certain, what is known from what is unknown, and pair this with a concrete resolution plan including specific test timelines, review points, safety-net instructions, escalation triggers, and named follow-up contacts so the patient does not carry the burden of uncertainty alone. Treat the conversation as an ongoing, patient-controlled dialogue by inviting questions, checking understanding, and making uncertainty actionable so patients can participate meaningfully in decisions without being overwhelmed by speculative open-ended differentials presented as equally probable.
integration_rationale: All three modifications share overlapping demands—patient preference assessment, structured most-likely framing, concrete next steps, and proportionality to clinical risk—which could be woven into a single coherent protocol without contradiction. Stakeholder C's proportionality guardrail was reconciled with Stakeholders A and B's emphasis on patient-controlled pacing by framing urgency as a contextual modifier rather than a reason to withhold, preserving the core synthesis direction of collaborative, transparent disclosure.
